```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
source(here("R", "analytic_merge.R"))
source(here("R", "tha-partner.R"))
theme_set(theme_gray(base_size = 16))
read_region <- function(region) {
  tag <- sprintf("EUR-%s-%%s-EUR%sOSN-20250601-20250614.csv", region, region)
  list(flights = read_csv(here("data", sprintf(tag, "flights")), show_col_types = FALSE),
       ms = read_milestones(here("data", sprintf(tag, "milestone"))))
}
bra <- read_region("BRA"); chn <- read_region("CHN"); zaf <- read_region("ZAF")
tha <- tha_read(); tha_lk <- tha_link_osn(tha)
core_mst <- c("SOBT", "AOBT", "ATOT", "D40", "D100", "A100", "A40", "ALDT", "AIBT", "SIBT")
hide_mst <- "^LVL|^FL\\d|^[AD](50|60|110|120)$|taxiway|parking|apron"
tb <- function(x, n = 0) flextable::flextable(mutate(x, across(where(is.double), \(v) round(v, n)))) |>
  flextable::fontsize(size = 12, part = "all") |> flextable::autofit()
pc <- \(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 1)
```

## Why we are here

- PBWG compares operational performance **across regions**.
- International flights connect the regions – but **no single source** observes them from off-block to in-block.
- TN-01 shows how to merge the pieces into one **analytic milestone dataset**.

## What we ask the PBWG

1. Adopt the **analytic milestone dataset** as the common first layer of PBWG analyses.
2. Agree the **milestone-table format** for partner contributions.
3. **Complement the dataset** with your milestone lists.

## A PBWG study dataset

| Work thread | Uses the dataset for |
|---|---|
| TN-01 milestone dataset | linking all sources per flight |
| TN-02 turnaround | delay one leg either side of a turn |
| TN-03 TBO delivery | offsets at contract points |
| VFE (exploratory) | level-offs near airports |

::: {.notes}
One dataset, several work threads. Each thread adds a payload and an algorithm on top of the same milestone table.
:::

## Outline

1. The problem: one flight, many pieces
2. Method: three layers, three linkage steps
3. Examples: Europe–Brazil, Europe–China
4. What the merged data show
5. Between non-European regions
6. Partner contributions: DECEA, CAAC/CAUC, AEROTHAI
7. Data requirements and how to contribute

# 1. The problem

## Each source covers one part

- **European airport data (APDF):** the European end.
- **Partner data:** the partner end.
- **OpenSky Network (OSN):** wherever its volunteer receivers see the aircraft.
- Over the ocean: **nobody**.

## OSN: a flight in pieces

- OSN loses the aircraft over the ocean and starts a **new segment** when it sees it again.
- Only the first segment has the departure airport, only the last the destination.
- Linking needs the **aircraft identity (ICAO24) and time**, not the airport pair.

# 2. Method

## Three layers

| Layer | Content |
|---|---|
| 1\. Analytic dataset | all milestones, all sources, linked per flight |
| 2\. Payload | metric-specific cleaning and selection |
| 3\. Algorithm | metric calculation (taxi, ASMA, VFE, ...) |

## Keep everything

- **No de-duplication, no overwriting, no source ranking.**
- Every row stays traceable to its source (`SOURCE`, `SOURCE_ID`).
- Which source is more trustworthy for a milestone is a **payload decision**.

## Three linkage steps

| Step | Rule |
|---|---|
| 1\. Reference records → flight | same ICAO24, ADEP, ADES; arrival within block-time window |
| 2\. OSN segments → flight | same ICAO24; overlaps flight window |
| 3\. Merge | all events of the linked segments |

::: {.notes}
Only mutually unique pairs are linked. One-sided flights keep their single reference record. MATCH records how each row was attached.
:::

# 3. Examples

## TAM8085 London–São Paulo

```{r}
ex <- "EGLL-SBGR-E48BA9-202506072034"
bra$ms |>
  filter(UID == ex, !str_detect(MST, hide_mst)) |>
  mutate(SOURCE = factor(SOURCE, c("OSN", "BRA", "EUR"), c("OSN", "Brazil", "Europe (APDF)")),
         milestone = if_else(MST %in% core_mst, "PBWG milestone", "other OSN event")) |>
  ggplot(aes(TIME, SOURCE)) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = milestone), size = 3) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("PBWG milestone" = 16, "other OSN event" = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Time (UTC), 7–8 June 2025", y = NULL, shape = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: {.notes}
APDF: SOBT, AOBT, ATOT, D40, D100 at EGLL. Brazil: A100, A40, ALDT, AIBT, SIBT at SBGR. OSN: runway times at both ends, rings at EGLL, A40 at SBGR, vertical profile, three segments. Where two sources report the same milestone: within 4 s (D40) to 53 s (ALDT).
:::

## Takeaway: complementary sources

- Neither reference source alone covers **AOBT → AIBT**.
- Merged, the flight is complete; OSN adds the airborne profile.
- Where sources overlap, they agree **within reporting precision**.

# 4. What the merged data show

## Region pairs, 1–14 June 2025

```{r}
map2(list(bra, chn, zaf), c("Europe–Brazil", "Europe–China", "Europe–South Africa"), \(x, r)
  x$flights |> summarise(`Region pair` = r, Flights = n(), `Both ends` = pc(mean(LINK == "dep+arr")),
                         `With OSN` = pc(mean(N_OSN_SEGMENTS > 0)))) |>
  list_rbind() |> tb()
```

::: {.notes}
South Africa: no partner data yet – APDF + OSN baseline. Both ends = linked reference records at both ends.
:::

## Takeaway: partner data matter

- OSN links to **practically all** flights – but near partner airports it sees little.
- São Paulo: 40 NM ring for about a third of arrivals, **almost no runway times**.
- China: very limited open coverage – **partner data are the primary source**.
- Agreement OSN vs APDF runway times: median **below 30 s**.

# 5. Between non-European regions

## Reconstructed from OSN alone

- Japan–USA, Singapore–Thailand, ...: no European record.
- Flights are rebuilt by **chaining OSN segments per aircraft** in time.
- Conservative: exclude rather than merge two flights.
- Result: a **baseline** that both partners of a pair can complete.

# 6. Partner contributions

## Thank you, partners

| Partner | Contribution |
|---|---|
| **DECEA** (Brazil) | Brazilian end of Europe–Brazil flights; block, runway, schedule, arrival 40/100 NM rings |
| **CAAC, CAUC** (China) | Chinese end of Europe–China flights; block, runway, schedule times |
| **AEROTHAI** (Thailand) | Thai domestic, Thailand–Singapore/Japan; block, runway, 40/100 NM rings |

::: {.notes}
All three in the PBWG milestone format. Brazil and China complete the partner end of flights to and from Europe; AEROTHAI is the first contribution between two non-European regions.
:::

## AEROTHAI milestones

- About **`r format(round(n_distinct(tha$SOURCE_ID), -3), big.mark = ",")` flights**, June–September 2025.
- Thai domestic, Thailand–Singapore, Thailand–Japan.
- AOBT, ATOT, D40, D100, A100, A40, ALDT, AIBT – in the **PBWG format**.
- First partner data between **two non-European regions**.

## Linked to the OSN baseline

- `r nrow(tha_lk$link)` of `r nrow(tha_lk$osn)` OSN flights Thailand–Singapore/Japan link to AEROTHAI (**`r pc(nrow(tha_lk$link) / nrow(tha_lk$osn))`**).
- Link on aircraft identification, airports and time (no registration in the file).
- Median time difference **below one minute**.

## The Thai end, completed

```{r}
tha_osn_coverage(tha, tha_lk$link) |>
  mutate(MST = factor(MST, c("AOBT", "ATOT", "D40", "D100", "A100", "A40", "ALDT", "AIBT"))) |>
  pivot_longer(c(OSN, AEROTHAI), names_to = "Source") |>
  ggplot(aes(MST, value, fill = Source)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "share of flights", fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

::: {.notes}
1–13 June 2025, linked flights. OSN sees the airborne milestones near Bangkok well but block times for only about a quarter to a third of the flights; AEROTHAI completes them. Runway times agree within about half a minute (OSN take-off ~30 s after the AEROTHAI ATOT – a definition difference, not a linkage error).
:::

## Takeaway: AEROTHAI

- Open data see the air; **partner data see the ground**.
- With AEROTHAI, the Thai end is complete for practically every flight.
- Adding **scheduled times and registration** would open punctuality and turnaround analyses (TN-02).

# 7. Data requirements

## The milestone table

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| FLTID, REG, ICAO24, TYPE | flight and aircraft identity |
| ADEP, ADES | airports |
| MST, MST_LBL | milestone; runway / stand |
| TIME, LAT, LON, ALT | value (UTC) |
| SOURCE, SOURCE_ID | provider and record id |

## Minimum to start

- **Core milestones:** SOBT, AOBT, ATOT, ALDT, AIBT, SIBT at your airports.
- **Identity:** REG or ICAO24 – makes linkage robust.
- **Recommended:** D40/D100, A100/A40 ring crossings.
- One row per milestone, **UTC**, as delivered – no ranking needed.

## How members contribute

1. Provide a sample month in the milestone format.
2. PRU links it to European and OSN data and returns the merged dataset.
3. Agree payload rules per metric together.

::: {.notes}
Every contribution improves the dataset for all members: the partner end of European flights and the flights between partner regions.
:::

## Proposal

- Adopt the **analytic milestone dataset** as the PBWG common layer.
- Agree the **milestone format** (incl. REG/ICAO24) for contributions.
- Members **complement** the dataset with their milestone lists.
- Next: Singapore data, payload rules, D200/A200 rings.
